title.value: BONUS-BASED EXPLORATION METHODS IN THE ARCADE LEARNING ENVIRONMENT
title.justification: The title of the paper is explicitly stated at the beginning of the document.
title.quote: O N B ONUS -B ASED E XPLORATION M ETHODS IN THE A RCADE L EARNING E NVIRONMENT

analysis.description: The paper reassesses bonus-based exploration methods in reinforcement learning applied to Atari 2600 game-playing, evaluating their performance on Montezuma’s Revenge and other hard exploration games within a common framework to understand their efficacy.

type.justification: The study is empirical as it involves experiments and evaluations of different exploration methods on the Atari 2600 games, specifically on Montezuma's Revenge and others, to validate their performance.
type.quote: In this paper we reassess popular bonus-based exploration methods within a common evaluation framework.

name.justification: The paper focuses on exploration methods within the context of reinforcement learning, particularly in gaming environments like Atari 2600.
name.quote: Research on exploration in reinforcement learning, as applied to Atari 2600 game-playing, has emphasized tackling difficult exploration problems such as M ONTEZUMA ’ S REVENGE (Bellemare et al., 2016).

name.justification: The paper evaluates exploration methods that use deep learning approaches to improve reinforcement learning strategies, thus fitting into the Deep Reinforcement Learning subfield.
name.quote: One of the most successful approaches to exploration in deep reinforcement learning is to provide an exploration bonus based on the relative novelty of the state.

name.justification: The paper focuses on improving exploration methods for playing games, specifically Atari 2600, highlighting the application domain of game playing.
name.quote: Research on exploration in reinforcement learning, as applied to Atari 2600 game-playing, has emphasized tackling difficult exploration problems such as MONTEZUMA’S REVENGE (Bellemare et al., 2016).

name.justification: The Rainbow agent is explicitly mentioned as a model used in combination with exploration bonuses in the evaluation.
name.quote: We combine Rainbow (Hessel et al., 2018) with different exploration bonuses and evaluate its performance on M ONTEZUMA ’ S R EVENGE.

is_contributed.justification: Rainbow is used but not introduced or contributed by this paper. It is a pre-existing model that is applied in the research.
is_contributed.quote: We combine Rainbow (Hessel et al., 2018) with different exploration bonuses.

is_executed.justification: The Rainbow model is executed as part of the experiments evaluating its performance on different games.
is_executed.quote: We apply the Rainbow (Hessel et al., 2018) agent in turn to M ONTEZUMA ’ S R EVENGE, Bellemare et al.’s seven hardest Atari 2600 games for exploration, and the full suite from the ALE.

is_compared.justification: Rainbow is compared to other models and exploration bonuses to assess its performance and the impact of those bonuses.
is_compared.quote: We combine Rainbow (Hessel et al., 2018) with different exploration bonuses and evaluate its performance.

name.justification: The paper uses the entire suite of 60 available Atari 2600 games as a testbed for evaluating exploration methods.
name.quote: One of the original tenets of the ALE is that agent evaluation should take on the entire suite of 60 available Atari 2600 games.
